text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as oil prices spiked on escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, sending U.S. crude up sharply and pushing the stock higher alongside the broader energy sector. The company benefits directly when crude prices climb—higher oil prices mean higher revenues from its production and sales.

The move is part of a much larger two-week rally (up 15.6%) that reflects a fundamental tightening in oil supply. Beyond the immediate headlines about Iran, the data shows a significant gap between where crude trades ($102 U.S., $127 world) and its true cost to physically deliver—about $38 per barrel higher when you factor in soaring tanker rates to move the oil. That squeeze between benchmark prices and actual delivery costs is pushing real economic value into oil producers' hands, which is lifting the entire sector.
